q: In the very beginning, what did God create?
why: The Bible's first sentence tells us God made everything.
quote: In the beginning God created the heavens and the earth.

q: On the first day of creation, what did God make just by speaking?
why: God spoke, and light appeared.
quote: And God said, “Let there be light,” and there was light.

q: During creation, what name did God give the light?
why: God named the light and the darkness.
quote: God called the light “day,” and the darkness He called “night.”

q: On the fourth day of creation, what else did God make besides the two great lights?
why: God filled the sky with lights to mark days and seasons.
quote: And He made the stars as well.

q: During creation, in whose image did God create people?
why: People are special because they reflect God.
quote: So God created man in His own image

q: At the end of the sixth day, how did God describe everything He had made?
why: God was pleased with all He had made.
quote: and indeed, it was very good.

q: After creating everything, what did God do on the seventh day?
why: God finished His work and rested.
quote: so on that day He rested from all His work.

q: In the creation story, what did God form the first man from?
why: Then God breathed the breath of life into him.
quote: Then the LORD God formed man from the dust of the ground

q: In the creation story, what did God use to make the first woman?
why: God made a helper suitable for the man.
quote: And from the rib that the LORD God had taken from the man, He made a woman

q: In the Garden of Eden, which creature tricked the woman?
why: The serpent made her doubt what God had said.
quote: Now the serpent was more crafty than any beast of the field

q: In Eden, after the woman ate the forbidden fruit, who did she give some to?
why: Adam was with her, and he ate too.
quote: She also gave some to her husband who was with her, and he ate it.

q: After eating the forbidden fruit, what did Adam and Eve sew together to cover themselves?
why: Their eyes were opened and they felt ashamed.
quote: so they sewed together fig leaves and made coverings for themselves.

q: When Adam and Eve heard God walking in the garden, what did they do?
why: Sin made them afraid to face God.
quote: they hid themselves from the presence of the LORD God among the trees of the garden.

q: After Adam and Eve hid in the garden, what did God call out to Adam?
why: God came looking for them.
quote: But the LORD God called out to the man, “Where are you?”

q: When God asked Eve what she had done, whom did she blame?
why: Adam blamed Eve, and Eve blamed the serpent.
quote: “The serpent deceived me,” she replied, “and I ate.”

q: After the first sin, what name did Adam give his wife?
why: She would be the mother of all the living.
quote: And Adam named his wife Eve

q: After sending Adam and Eve out of Eden, what did God place to guard the tree of life?
why: The way back to the tree of life was closed.
quote: and stationed cherubim on the east side of the Garden of Eden, along with a whirling sword of flame

q: What job did Abel, Adam's son, have?
why: Abel was a shepherd; his brother Cain was a farmer.
quote: Now Abel was a keeper of sheep

q: What job did Cain, Adam's son, have?
why: Cain was a farmer; his brother Abel was a shepherd.
quote: while Cain was a tiller of the soil.

q: When Cain and Abel brought offerings, whose offering did God look on with favor?
why: Abel brought the best of his flock.
quote: And the LORD looked with favor on Abel and his offering

q: How did Cain feel when God did not accept his offering?
why: His anger led him to sin.
quote: So Cain became very angry, and his countenance fell.

q: Out in the field, what did Cain do to his brother Abel?
why: This was the first murder in the Bible.
quote: Cain rose up against his brother Abel and killed him.

q: When God asked Cain where Abel was, what did Cain answer?
why: Cain tried to hide what he had done.
quote: “Am I my brother’s keeper?”

q: After Cain killed Abel, what did God put on Cain to protect him?
why: The mark kept others from killing Cain.
quote: And the LORD placed a mark on Cain

q: When the world was full of evil, who found favor in the eyes of the LORD?
why: Noah walked with God in a wicked world.
quote: Noah, however, found favor in the eyes of the LORD.

q: Before the flood, how many sons did Noah have?
why: His sons were Shem, Ham, and Japheth.
quote: And Noah had three sons: Shem, Ham, and Japheth.

q: Before the flood, what did God tell Noah to build?
why: The ark would keep Noah's family and the animals alive.
quote: Make for yourself an ark of gopher wood

q: What kind of animal pairs did God tell Noah to bring into the ark?
why: The animals would fill the earth again after the flood.
quote: you are to bring two of every living creature into the ark—male and female

q: In Noah's flood, how long did the rain fall?
why: The waters covered even the high mountains.
quote: And the rain fell upon the earth for forty days and forty nights.

q: When the floodwaters went down, where did Noah's ark come to rest?
why: The ark settled as the waters slowly went down.
quote: the ark came to rest on the mountains of Ararat.

q: After the flood, what was the first bird Noah sent out of the ark?
why: Later Noah sent out a dove.
quote: and sent out a raven.

q: After the flood, what did the dove bring back to Noah in her beak?
why: Noah knew the waters had gone down.
quote: the dove returned to him in the evening with a freshly plucked olive leaf in her beak.

q: When Noah came out of the ark, what did he build?
why: Noah thanked God with burnt offerings.
quote: Then Noah built an altar to the LORD.

q: After the flood, what sign of His promise did God set in the clouds?
why: God promised never again to destroy the earth by a flood.
quote: I have set My rainbow in the clouds

q: Before the Tower of Babel, how many languages did the whole world speak?
why: Everyone could understand everyone else.
quote: Now the whole world had one language and a common form of speech.

q: When people built the Tower of Babel, what did they use instead of stone?
why: They baked bricks to build their city and tower.
quote: So they used brick instead of stone

q: Why did the people at Babel want a tower that reached to the heavens?
a: To make a name for themselves
why: They wanted fame and to stay together in one place.
quote: that we may make a name for ourselves

q: At the Tower of Babel, what did God do to the people's language?
why: They could no longer understand one another.
quote: Come, let Us go down and confuse their language

q: After God confused their language, what did the builders at Babel stop doing?
why: God scattered them over all the earth.
quote: and they stopped building the city.

q: What was the city with the unfinished tower called?
why: There the LORD confused the language of the whole world.
quote: That is why it is called Babel

q: In the Garden of Eden, which two trees stood in the middle of the garden?
a: Tree of life, tree of knowledge
wrong: A fig tree and a vine
why: God told Adam not to eat from the tree of knowledge.
quote: And in the middle of the garden were the tree of life and the tree of the knowledge of good and evil.

q: Why did God put the first man in the Garden of Eden?
why: From the start, God gave people good work to do.
quote: and placed him in the Garden of Eden to cultivate and keep it.

q: In the Garden of Eden, what did God say was not good?
a: For the man to be alone
wrong: For the garden to be empty
For the animals to be wild
why: So God made a suitable helper for him.
quote: It is not good for the man to be alone.

q: In the Garden of Eden, who gave names to all the animals?
why: God brought the animals to the man to name them.
quote: The man gave names to all the livestock

q: After the first sin, God told the serpent the woman's offspring would crush what?
why: This is the first promise that evil would be defeated.
quote: He will crush your head, and you will strike his heel.

q: After the first sin, God told Adam he would one day return to what?
why: Adam was made from the ground.
quote: For dust you are, and to dust you shall return.

q: After the first sin, what did God make to clothe Adam and Eve?
why: God cared for them even after they sinned.
quote: And the LORD God made garments of skin for Adam and his wife, and He clothed them.

q: When Cain was angry, God warned him that something was crouching at his door. What?
why: God told Cain he must master it.
quote: sin is crouching at your door

q: After killing Abel, where did Cain go to live?
why: Nod was east of Eden.
quote: and settled in the land of Nod, east of Eden.

q: After Abel died, what did Adam and Eve name their next son?
why: Eve said God had given her another child in place of Abel.
quote: she gave birth to a son and named him Seth

q: In the family line from Adam to Noah, who lived a total of 969 years?
why: He is the oldest person named in the Bible.
quote: So Methuselah lived a total of 969 years

q: Before the flood, which man walked with God and then was taken away by God?
why: Enoch did not die like the others in his family line.
quote: Enoch walked with God, and then he was no more, because God had taken him away.

q: What kind of wood did God tell Noah to use for the ark?
why: God gave Noah exact building instructions.
quote: Make for yourself an ark of gopher wood

q: How does Genesis describe Noah's character before the flood?
why: Noah walked with God.
quote: Noah was a righteous man, blameless in his generation

q: After the flood, God promised that as long as the earth lasts, what would never stop?
a: Seedtime and harvest, day and night
why: God promised a steady world after the flood.
quote: seedtime and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter, day and night shall never cease.

q: How long did God tell Noah to make the ark?
why: It was also 50 cubits wide and 30 cubits high.
quote: The ark is to be 300 cubits long

q: In Noah's flood, how long did the waters prevail on the earth?
why: The rain lasted forty days, but the water stayed much longer.
quote: And the waters prevailed upon the earth for 150 days.

q: How many pairs of each kind of clean animal did Noah take into the ark?
why: Unclean animals came in one pair each.
quote: You are to take with you seven pairs of every kind of clean animal

q: How old was Noah when the floodwaters burst forth?
why: It happened on the seventeenth day of the second month.
quote: In the six hundredth year of Noah’s life

q: Where did people settle before building the Tower of Babel?
a: A plain in the land of Shinar
why: They journeyed eastward and settled there.
quote: they found a plain in the land of Shinar and settled there.

q: After whom did Cain name the city he built?
why: This Enoch is not the Enoch who walked with God.
quote: Then Cain built a city and named it after his son Enoch.

q: When building at Babel, what did people use instead of mortar?
why: They also used brick instead of stone.
quote: and tar instead of mortar.

q: In the family line from Adam to Noah, how many years did Enoch live in all?
why: Then God took him away.
quote: So Enoch lived a total of 365 years.

q: When God called Abram, what did He tell him to leave behind?
why: God asked Abram to go to a land He would show him.
quote: Leave your country, your kindred, and your father’s household

q: When God called Abram, what did He promise to make him into?
why: God also promised to bless him.
quote: I will make you into a great nation

q: When Abram obeyed God's call and left Haran, which nephew went with him?
why: Abram took Sarai and Lot with him.
quote: and Lot went with him.

q: When Abram obeyed God's call, which land did he set out for?
why: This was the land God promised to his offspring.
quote: and set out for the land of Canaan.

q: When God appeared to Abram in Canaan, what did Abram build there?
why: Abram worshiped the God who had spoken to him.
quote: So Abram built an altar there to the LORD

q: When God called Abram, who did He say would be blessed through him?
a: All the families of the earth
why: God's plan for Abram reached the whole world.
quote: and all the families of the earth will be blessed through you.

q: When God gave childless Abram a promise at night, what did He tell him to count?
why: Abram's offspring would be as many as the stars.
quote: Now look to the heavens and count the stars, if you are able.

q: In a vision, God told Abram, “Do not be afraid. I am your…” what?
why: God promised to protect Abram and be his reward.
quote: I am your shield, your very great reward.

q: When God promised Abram offspring like the stars, how did Abram respond?
why: God counted Abram's faith as righteousness.
quote: Abram believed the LORD, and it was credited to him as righteousness.

q: Before God's promise of offspring like the stars, what was Abram worried about?
why: A servant was going to inherit everything.
quote: since I remain childless

q: God promised childless Abram that his heir would be whom?
why: God promised Abram a child of his own.
quote: but one who comes from your own body will be your heir.

q: When two angels came to Sodom in the evening, who was sitting in the city gateway?
why: Lot got up to meet them and bowed down.
quote: and Lot was sitting in the gateway of the city.

q: At daybreak in Sodom, what did the angels urge Lot to do?
wrong: Fight the men of the city
why: The city was about to be destroyed.
quote: Take your wife and your two daughters who are here

q: As Lot's family fled Sodom, what did the angels tell them not to do?
why: They had to run for their lives to the mountains.
quote: Do not look back

q: What did the LORD rain down on Sodom and Gomorrah?
why: God judged the wicked cities.
quote: Then the LORD rained down sulfur and fire on Sodom and Gomorrah

q: When Lot's wife looked back at Sodom, what did she become?
why: She did not obey the angels' warning.
quote: But Lot’s wife looked back, and she became a pillar of salt.

q: When Lot hesitated to leave Sodom, what did the angels do?
a: Took their hands and led them out
why: The LORD had compassion on Lot's family.
quote: the men grabbed his hand and the hands of his wife and his two daughters.

q: What did Abraham name the son that Sarah bore him in their old age?
why: God kept His promise to Abraham and Sarah.
quote: And Abraham gave the name Isaac to the son Sarah bore to him.

q: How old was Abraham when his son Isaac was born?
why: Nothing is too hard for the LORD.
quote: Abraham was a hundred years old when his son Isaac was born to him.

q: After Isaac was born, what did Sarah say God had made her do?
why: Her laugh of doubt became a laugh of joy.
quote: God has made me laugh

q: What did Abraham hold on the day his son Isaac was weaned?
why: The family celebrated the promised child.
quote: and Abraham held a great feast on the day Isaac was weaned.

q: When Hagar and her boy ran out of water in the wilderness, what did God show her?
why: God heard the boy's voice and cared for them.
quote: Then God opened her eyes, and she saw a well of water.

q: When was Isaac born to Abraham and Sarah?
a: At the very time God promised
why: God did exactly what He had said.
quote: at the very time God had promised.

q: When God tested Abraham, whom did He tell him to offer?
why: God was testing Abraham's trust.
quote: your only son Isaac, whom you love

q: When God tested Abraham, which land did He send him to?
why: God would show him one of the mountains there.
quote: and go to the land of Moriah.

q: As Abraham and Isaac walked up the mountain, what did Isaac carry?
why: Abraham carried the fire and the knife.
quote: Abraham took the wood for the burnt offering and placed it on his son Isaac.

q: On the way up the mountain, what did Isaac ask his father Abraham?
why: Isaac saw the fire and wood but no lamb.
quote: but where is the lamb for the burnt offering?

q: When Isaac asked where the lamb was, what did Abraham answer?
why: Abraham trusted God to provide.
quote: God Himself will provide the lamb for the burnt offering, my son.

q: Just as Abraham took the knife on the mountain, who called out to stop him?
why: Abraham had shown that he feared God.
quote: Just then the angel of the LORD called out to him from heaven

q: On the mountain, what did Abraham offer in place of his son Isaac?
a: A ram caught in a thicket
why: God provided a ram, caught by its horns.
quote: and saw behind him a ram in a thicket, caught by its horns.

q: In his old age, Abraham sent his servant to find a wife for whom?
why: The wife was to come from Abraham's own relatives.
quote: to take a wife for my son Isaac.

q: What animals did Abraham's servant take on his trip to find a wife for Isaac?
why: He also took many good gifts from his master.
quote: Then the servant took ten of his master’s camels

q: Looking for a wife for Isaac, where did Abraham's servant stop his camels to pray?
a: By a well outside the town
why: It was the time women came to draw water.
quote: he made the camels kneel down near the well outside the town

q: While Abraham's servant was still praying at the well, who came out with her jar?
why: God answered before he finished praying.
quote: Before the servant had finished praying, Rebekah came out with her jar on her shoulder.

q: At the well, what did Rebekah offer to do for the camels of Abraham's servant?
why: This was the sign the servant had prayed for.
quote: I will also draw water for your camels, until they have had enough to drink.

q: When her family asked Rebekah if she would go with Abraham's servant to marry Isaac, what did she say?
why: Rebekah chose to go to Isaac.
quote: “I will go,” she replied.

q: How did Isaac feel about Rebekah after he married her?
why: She comforted him after his mother's death.
quote: And Isaac loved her and was comforted after his mother’s death.

q: When Rebekah, Isaac's wife, gave birth, what was special about her children?
why: The twins were Esau and Jacob.
quote: there were indeed twins in her womb.

q: Which of Isaac's twins was born first, red and hairy?
why: He was covered with hair like a fur coat.
quote: The first one came out red, covered with hair like a fur coat; so they named him Esau.

q: When Jacob was born right after his twin, what was he holding on to?
why: That is how he got the name Jacob.
quote: his brother came out grasping Esau’s heel

q: When Isaac's twins grew up, what kind of man was Esau?
why: Jacob was the quiet one who stayed at home.
quote: Esau became a skillful hunter

q: One day Esau came in from the field very hungry. What was Jacob cooking?
why: Esau begged for some of the red stew.
quote: while Jacob was cooking some stew

q: What did Jacob ask Esau to sell him for a bowl of stew?
why: Esau traded something precious for one meal.
quote: “First sell me your birthright,” Jacob replied.

q: Which of the twin brothers did their mother Rebekah love?
why: Isaac loved Esau, but Rebekah loved Jacob.
quote: but Rebekah loved Jacob.

q: How old was Abram when he left Haran at God's call?
why: Abram obeyed God even in old age.
quote: Abram was seventy-five years old when he left Haran.

q: When a severe famine struck Canaan, where did Abram go to live for a while?
why: There was not enough food in the land.
quote: So Abram went down to Egypt to live there for a while because the famine was severe.

q: When Abram and Lot separated, which land did Lot choose for himself?
why: It looked well watered like the garden of the LORD.
quote: So Lot chose the whole plain of the Jordan for himself

q: After separating from Abram, Lot pitched his tent toward which city?
why: Lot moved near the wicked city of Sodom.
quote: and pitched his tent toward Sodom.

q: Which king of Salem brought bread and wine to Abram?
why: He was priest of God Most High.
quote: Then Melchizedek king of Salem brought out bread and wine

q: After Melchizedek blessed him, what did Abram give Melchizedek?
why: Abram honored the priest of God Most High.
quote: Then Abram gave Melchizedek a tenth of everything.

q: What was the name of Sarai's Egyptian maidservant?
why: Sarai gave Hagar to Abram because she had no children.
quote: but she had an Egyptian maidservant named Hagar.

q: What did Abram name the son that Hagar bore him?
why: Ishmael was born before Isaac.
quote: and Abram gave the name Ishmael to the son she had borne.

q: When God made His covenant with Abram, what new name did He give him?
why: His new name meant he would be a father of many nations.
quote: but your name will be Abraham, for I have made you a father of many nations.

q: When God renamed Abraham, what new name did He give Abraham's wife Sarai?
why: God promised she would be the mother of nations.
quote: for her name is to be Sarah.

q: When God appeared to Abram at age ninety-nine, what name did He call Himself?
why: God told Abram to walk before Him and be blameless.
quote: I am God Almighty.

q: By the Oaks of Mamre, how many men did Abraham see standing near his tent?
why: Abraham ran to welcome his visitors.
quote: And Abraham looked up and saw three men standing nearby.

q: When Sarah overheard that she would have a son in her old age, what did she do?
why: She thought she was too old.
quote: So she laughed to herself

q: When Sarah laughed at the promise of a son, what did the LORD ask Abraham?
a: Is anything too difficult for the LORD?
why: God promised Sarah would have a son in about a year.
quote: Is anything too difficult for the LORD?

q: When Abraham pleaded for Sodom, what was the smallest number of righteous people he asked about?
why: God said He would spare the city for ten.
quote: Suppose ten are found there?

q: What did Abraham name the mountain where God provided a ram in Isaac's place?
why: God had provided the sacrifice.
quote: And Abraham called that place The LORD Will Provide.

q: After Abraham's test on the mountain, God promised to multiply his descendants like what?
why: Abraham had not held back his only son.
quote: I will multiply your descendants like the stars in the sky and the sand on the seashore.

q: What was the name of Rebekah's brother, who rushed out to meet Abraham's servant?
why: Bethuel was her father; Laban was her brother.
quote: Now Rebekah had a brother named Laban

q: What was Isaac doing in the field when Rebekah's camels came into view?
why: He looked up and saw the camels approaching.
quote: Isaac went out to the field to meditate

q: Because he asked for the red stew, what other name was Esau given?
why: Edom sounds like the word for red.
quote: (That is why he was also called Edom.)

q: What did Jacob give Esau in exchange for his birthright?
why: Esau ate, drank, and went away.
quote: Then Jacob gave some bread and lentil stew to Esau

q: Before Rebekah's twins were born, what did God say about the older and the younger?
a: The older will serve the younger
wrong: The younger will serve the older
They will live apart in peace
why: God told her two nations were in her womb.
quote: and the older will serve the younger.

q: Where did Hagar wander with her son after Abraham sent them away?
why: Abraham gave her bread and a skin of water.
quote: She left and wandered in the Wilderness of Beersheba.

q: In Canaan, Abram traveled as far as the Oak of Moreh at which place?
why: There the LORD appeared to him.
quote: as far as the site of the Oak of Moreh at Shechem.

q: In Canaan, Abram pitched his tent with Bethel to the west and which town to the east?
why: There he built another altar to the LORD.
quote: with Bethel to the west and Ai to the east.

q: Before Isaac was born, who did Abram say would inherit his house?
why: Abram had no child of his own yet.
quote: and the heir of my house is Eliezer of Damascus?

q: How long had Abram lived in Canaan when Sarai gave him Hagar as a wife?
why: Sarai still had no children.
quote: So after he had lived in Canaan for ten years

q: At what age did Abraham circumcise his son Isaac?
why: Abraham did as God had commanded him.
quote: When his son Isaac was eight days old, Abraham circumcised him

q: How old was Abraham's wife Sarah when she died?
why: She died in Hebron in the land of Canaan.
quote: Now Sarah lived to be 127 years old.

q: Where did Abraham bury his wife Sarah?
why: The cave was near Mamre, that is, Hebron.
quote: Abraham buried his wife Sarah in the cave of the field at Machpelah near Mamre

q: How many years did Abraham live in all?
why: He died old and contented.
quote: Abraham lived a total of 175 years.

q: How old was Isaac when he married Rebekah?
why: Rebekah was the sister of Laban the Aramean.
quote: and Isaac was forty years old when he married Rebekah

q: How old was Isaac when his twin sons Esau and Jacob were born?
why: Isaac had prayed for his wife because she was barren.
quote: And Isaac was sixty years old when the twins were born.

q: Looking for a wife for Isaac, Abraham's servant set out for Nahor's hometown in which region?
why: Abraham's relatives lived there.
quote: And he set out for Nahor’s hometown in Aram-naharaim.

q: When God promised Abraham a son by Sarah, how old did Abraham say Sarah was?
why: Abraham himself was nearly a hundred.
quote: Can Sarah give birth at the age of ninety?

q: On his way to Haran, what did Jacob use as a pillow when he slept?
why: He stopped for the night because the sun had set.
quote: And taking one of the stones from that place, he put it under his head and lay down to sleep.

q: Sleeping on his way to Haran, what did Jacob dream about?
why: The ladder rested on the earth and reached heaven.
quote: And Jacob had a dream about a ladder that rested on the earth with its top reaching up to heaven

q: In Jacob's dream on the way to Haran, who was going up and down the ladder?
why: At the top stood the LORD Himself.
quote: and God’s angels were going up and down the ladder.

q: In Jacob's ladder dream, what did God promise to do wherever Jacob went?
why: God promised to bring Jacob back to the land.
quote: Look, I am with you, and I will watch over you wherever you go

q: When Jacob woke from his ladder dream, what did he say about that place?
a: Surely the LORD is in this place
why: Jacob had not known God was there.
quote: Surely the LORD is in this place, and I was unaware of it.

q: After his ladder dream, what did Jacob do with the stone he had slept on?
a: Set it up as a pillar
wrong: Used it to build a house
why: He poured oil on it to mark the place.
quote: and he set it up as a pillar. He poured oil on top of it

q: What name did Jacob give the place where he dreamed of the ladder?
why: Bethel means house of God.
quote: and he called that place Bethel

q: The night before Jacob met Esau again, what happened when Jacob was left alone?
why: They wrestled through the night.
quote: So Jacob was left all alone, and there a man wrestled with him until daybreak.

q: On the night before meeting Esau, how long did the man wrestle with Jacob?
why: Jacob would not give up.
quote: a man wrestled with him until daybreak.

q: When the man he wrestled said, “Let me go,” what did Jacob answer?
why: Jacob wanted God's blessing.
quote: I will not let you go unless you bless me.

q: After wrestling all night, what new name was Jacob given?
why: He had struggled with God and with men and prevailed.
quote: Your name will no longer be Jacob, but Israel

q: After wrestling with the man until daybreak, how did Jacob walk?
why: The man had struck his hip.
quote: and he was limping because of his hip.

q: Why did Jacob name the place where he wrestled Peniel?
a: He had seen God face to face
why: Jacob was amazed his life was spared.
quote: Indeed, I have seen God face to face, and yet my life was spared.

q: When Isaac was old and ready to bless his son, what was wrong with his eyes?
a: They were too weak to see
why: Because he could not see, Jacob could trick him.
quote: When Isaac was old and his eyes were so weak that he could no longer see

q: When old Isaac planned to bless Esau, what did he first ask Esau to do?
why: Isaac wanted a tasty meal before giving the blessing.
quote: go out into the field to hunt some game for me.

q: To trick blind Isaac, what did Rebekah put on Jacob's hands and neck?
why: Esau was hairy, and Jacob was smooth.
quote: She also put the skins of the young goats on his hands and on the smooth part of his neck.

q: When blind Isaac touched Jacob, what did he say about the voice and the hands?
why: Isaac was unsure but blessed Jacob anyway.
quote: The voice is the voice of Jacob, but the hands are the hands of Esau.

q: When Esau planned to kill Jacob over the stolen blessing, where did Rebekah tell Jacob to flee?
a: To her brother Laban in Haran
why: She wanted Jacob safe until Esau calmed down.
quote: flee at once to my brother Laban in Haran.

q: When Jacob reached Haran, who arrived at the well with her father's sheep?
why: Rachel was a shepherdess.
quote: Rachel arrived with her father’s sheep, for she was a shepherdess.

q: When Jacob first saw Rachel at the well in Haran, what did he do for her?
a: Rolled the stone away, watered her sheep
why: Rachel was the daughter of his uncle Laban.
quote: he went up and rolled the stone away from the mouth of the well and watered his uncle’s sheep.

q: How many years did Jacob offer to work for Laban to marry Rachel?
why: Jacob loved Rachel.
quote: I will serve you seven years for your younger daughter Rachel.

q: How did Jacob's seven years of work for Rachel feel to him?
why: His love for her made the time fly.
quote: yet it seemed but a few days because of his love for her.

q: After working seven years for Rachel, whom did Jacob find he had married?
why: Laban had tricked Jacob.
quote: When morning came, there was Leah!

q: What were the names of Laban's two daughters?
why: Leah was older and Rachel was younger.
quote: the older was named Leah, and the younger was named Rachel.

q: What did Rachel name her first son?
why: God remembered Rachel and gave her a son.
quote: She named him Joseph

q: When Jacob returned home, how many men were coming with Esau to meet him?
why: Jacob was greatly afraid.
quote: he and four hundred men with him.

q: When Esau finally met Jacob again after many years, what did Esau do?
why: The brothers wept together.
quote: Esau, however, ran to him and embraced him

q: As Jacob approached Esau after many years apart, how many times did he bow to the ground?
why: Jacob came humbly to his brother.
quote: and bowed to the ground seven times as he approached his brother.

q: As Rachel was dying in childbirth, what name did Jacob give her newborn son?
why: Rachel had named him Ben-oni.
quote: But his father called him Benjamin.

q: How many sons did Jacob have in all?
why: They became the twelve tribes of Israel.
quote: Jacob had twelve sons:

q: What did Isaac name the well that no one quarreled over?
why: Isaac said the LORD had made room for them.
quote: He named it Rehoboth

q: Before Jacob named it Bethel, what was that city called?
why: Jacob renamed it after his ladder dream.
quote: though previously the city had been named Luz.

q: At Bethel, how much of all God gave him did Jacob vow to give back?
why: Jacob made a vow after his dream.
quote: and of all that You give me I will surely give You a tenth.

q: Which servant girl did Laban give to his daughter Leah as her maidservant?
why: Bilhah was given to Rachel.
quote: And Laban gave his servant girl Zilpah to his daughter Leah as her maidservant.

q: How many years in all did Jacob serve in Laban's household?
why: Fourteen years for his wives and six for his flocks.
quote: Thus for twenty years I have served in your household

q: Jacob complained that his uncle Laban had changed his wages how many times?
why: Laban kept cheating Jacob.
quote: and you have changed my wages ten times!

q: When angels met Jacob on his way home, what did he name that place?
why: He called it the camp of God.
quote: So he named that place Mahanaim.

q: The night before meeting Esau, which stream did Jacob's family cross?
why: Then Jacob was left alone.
quote: and crossed the ford of the Jabbok.

q: Where was Jacob's wife Rachel buried?
why: Ephrath is Bethlehem.
quote: So Rachel died and was buried on the way to Ephrath (that is, Bethlehem).

q: Who was Jacob's firstborn son?
why: Reuben was Leah's first son.
quote: The sons of Leah were Reuben the firstborn of Jacob

q: What special gift did Jacob make for his son Joseph?
why: Jacob loved Joseph more than his other sons.
quote: so he made him a robe of many colors.

q: Why did Joseph's brothers hate him?
why: They could not even speak a kind word to him.
quote: When Joseph’s brothers saw that their father loved him more than any of them, they hated him

q: In young Joseph's first dream, what bowed down to his sheaf of grain?
why: His brothers hated him even more after this dream.
quote: while your sheaves gathered around and bowed down to mine.

q: In young Joseph's second dream, what was bowing down to him?
a: The sun, moon, and eleven stars
why: Even his father wondered about this dream.
quote: the sun and moon and eleven stars were bowing down to me.

q: When Joseph's brothers saw him coming in the fields, what did they call him?
why: They were angry about his dreams.
quote: “Here comes that dreamer!” they said to one another.

q: After taking his colorful robe, where did Joseph's brothers throw him?
why: The pit had no water in it.
quote: and they took him and threw him into the pit. Now the pit was empty, with no water in it.

q: Who did Joseph's jealous brothers sell him to?
why: The traders took Joseph to Egypt.
quote: and sold him for twenty shekels of silver to the Ishmaelites, who took him to Egypt.

q: After selling Joseph, what did his brothers dip his robe in to fool their father?
why: They wanted Jacob to think an animal had killed Joseph.
quote: slaughtered a young goat, and dipped the robe in its blood.

q: In Pharaoh's first dream, what came up out of the Nile?
why: Then seven thin cows came up after them.
quote: when seven cows, sleek and well-fed, came up from the river

q: In Pharaoh's dream by the Nile, what did the thin cows do to the fat cows?
why: Then Pharaoh woke up troubled.
quote: And the cows that were sickly and thin devoured the seven sleek, well-fed cows.

q: When Pharaoh asked Joseph to explain his dream, who did Joseph say would give the answer?
why: Joseph gave God the credit.
quote: but God will give Pharaoh a sound answer.

q: Joseph said Pharaoh's dreams meant seven years of plenty followed by what?
why: Egypt needed to store food during the good years.
quote: but seven years of famine will follow them.

q: After Joseph explained the dreams, what did Pharaoh put him in charge of?
why: Pharaoh saw that God's Spirit was in Joseph.
quote: I hereby place you over all the land of Egypt.

q: When Pharaoh put Joseph in charge of Egypt, what did he put on Joseph's finger?
why: The ring showed Joseph had Pharaoh's authority.
quote: Then Pharaoh removed the signet ring from his finger, put it on Joseph’s finger

q: During the great famine, why did every nation come to Joseph in Egypt?
why: Joseph had stored grain during the good years.
quote: And every nation came to Joseph in Egypt to buy grain

q: When Joseph finally told his brothers in Egypt who he was, what did he say?
why: He also asked if his father was still alive.
quote: Joseph said to his brothers, “I am Joseph! Is my father still alive?”

q: When Joseph revealed who he was, how did his brothers feel?
why: They could not even answer him.
quote: because they were terrified in his presence.

q: When Joseph made himself known to his brothers, how loudly did he weep?
why: Even Pharaoh's household heard about it.
quote: But he wept so loudly that the Egyptians heard him

q: Joseph told his brothers that God sent him to Egypt ahead of them for what reason?
why: Joseph saw God's plan in all that happened.
quote: because it was to save lives that God sent me before you.

q: Joseph told his brothers who had really sent him to Egypt. Who?
why: God had made him ruler over Egypt.
quote: Therefore it was not you who sent me here, but God

q: In which region of Egypt did Joseph invite his family to settle?
why: There they could be near Joseph.
quote: You shall settle in the land of Goshen and be near me

q: When old Jacob heard that Joseph was alive, what did he decide?
a: To go see him before he died
why: Jacob had mourned Joseph for many years.
quote: My son Joseph is still alive! I will go to see him before I die.

q: How old was Joseph when he was tending the flock with his brothers?
why: He brought his father a bad report about his brothers.
quote: When Joseph was seventeen years old, he was tending the flock with his brothers

q: Which brother tried to save Joseph by telling the others to throw him in a pit instead of killing him?
why: Reuben planned to bring Joseph back to their father.
quote: Reuben said this so that he could rescue Joseph from their hands and return him to his father.

q: Which brother suggested selling Joseph instead of killing him?
why: He said there was no profit in killing their brother.
quote: Then Judah said to his brothers, “What profit will we gain if we kill our brother and cover up his blood?

q: For how much silver did Joseph's brothers sell him?
why: The traders took Joseph down to Egypt.
quote: and sold him for twenty shekels of silver

q: In Egypt, who bought Joseph from the Ishmaelites?
why: Potiphar was an officer of Pharaoh.
quote: an Egyptian named Potiphar, an officer of Pharaoh and captain of the guard, bought him

q: Why did Joseph succeed while serving in Potiphar's house?
why: Potiphar put him in charge of everything he owned.
quote: And the LORD was with Joseph, and he became a successful man

q: When Potiphar's wife grabbed Joseph by his cloak, what did Joseph do?
a: Left the cloak and ran outside
why: Joseph refused to sin against God.
quote: But leaving his cloak in her hand, he escaped and ran outside.

q: While Joseph was in prison, what did the warden put him in charge of?
why: The LORD gave Joseph success even in prison.
quote: And the warden put all the prisoners under Joseph’s care

q: Which two officers of Pharaoh ended up in prison with Joseph?
a: The chief cupbearer and chief baker
wrong: The chief priest and a scribe
why: Pharaoh was angry with them.
quote: the chief cupbearer and the chief baker

q: In prison, Joseph said the three branches in the cupbearer's dream meant what?
why: In three days the cupbearer got his job back.
quote: The three branches are three days.

q: After the cupbearer was set free from prison, what did he do about Joseph?
why: Joseph stayed in prison two more years.
quote: The chief cupbearer, however, did not remember Joseph; he forgot all about him.

q: In Pharaoh's second dream, what had scorched the thin heads of grain?
why: The thin heads swallowed the plump ones.
quote: thin and scorched by the east wind.

q: How old was Joseph when he entered Pharaoh's service?
why: Thirteen years had passed since he was sold.
quote: Now Joseph was thirty years old when he entered the service of Pharaoh king of Egypt.

q: What did Joseph name his firstborn son in Egypt?
why: Joseph said God had made him forget his hardship.
quote: Joseph named the firstborn Manasseh

q: During the famine, how many of Joseph's brothers first went to Egypt to buy grain?
why: Benjamin stayed home with Jacob.
quote: So ten of Joseph’s brothers went down to buy grain from Egypt.

q: Which brother did Jacob keep at home when the others first went to Egypt for grain?
why: Jacob was afraid harm might come to him.
quote: But Jacob did not send Joseph’s brother Benjamin with his brothers

q: When Joseph's brothers came to Egypt to buy grain, did they recognize him?
why: Joseph recognized them, but he looked like an Egyptian ruler.
quote: Although Joseph recognized his brothers, they did not recognize him.

q: Which of his brothers did Joseph keep bound in Egypt?
why: The others had to go home and bring Benjamin.
quote: he took Simeon from them and had him bound before their eyes.

q: Whose grain sack did Joseph order his silver cup to be hidden in?
why: The youngest brother was Benjamin.
quote: Put my cup, the silver one, in the mouth of the youngest one’s sack

q: At the end of Genesis, what did Joseph tell his brothers about the evil they had planned against him?
why: God used it to save many lives.
quote: As for you, what you intended against me for evil, God intended for good

q: When Jacob came down to Egypt, what did Joseph do when he met his father?
why: Father and son were together again after many years.
quote: Joseph presented himself to him, embraced him, and wept profusely.

q: When Joseph was sold, what were the traders' camels carrying down to Egypt?
why: The caravan was coming from Gilead.
quote: Their camels were carrying spices, balm, and myrrh on their way down to Egypt.

q: What was Potiphar's position in Egypt?
why: He was an officer of Pharaoh.
quote: an officer of Pharaoh and captain of the guard.

q: In the chief baker's dream in prison, how many baskets were on his head?
why: Joseph said the three baskets were three days.
quote: There were three baskets of white bread on my head.

q: On what occasion were Pharaoh's cupbearer and baker brought out of prison?
why: Pharaoh held a feast for all his officials.
quote: On the third day, which was Pharaoh’s birthday

q: How long after the cupbearer's release did Pharaoh have his troubling dream?
why: Then the cupbearer finally remembered Joseph.
quote: After two full years had passed, Pharaoh had a dream

q: What Egyptian name did Pharaoh give Joseph?
why: Joseph took charge of all the land of Egypt.
quote: Pharaoh gave Joseph the name Zaphenath-paneah

q: Whom did Pharaoh give Joseph as his wife?
why: Her father was priest of On.
quote: and he gave him Asenath daughter of Potiphera, priest of On, to be his wife.

q: What did Joseph name his second son in Egypt?
why: Joseph said God had made him fruitful.
quote: And the second son he named Ephraim

q: When Jacob met Pharaoh in Egypt, how old did he say he was?
why: Jacob said his years had been few and hard.
quote: “My travels have lasted 130 years,” Jacob replied.

q: How old was Jacob when his life ended in Egypt?
why: He lived seventeen years in Egypt.
quote: and the length of his life was 147 years.

q: How old was Joseph when he died in Egypt?
why: His body was placed in a coffin in Egypt.
quote: So Joseph died at the age of 110.

q: In Jacob's blessing of his sons, from which son would the scepter not depart?
why: Kings would come from Judah's line.
quote: The scepter will not depart from Judah

q: When Joseph rode in Pharaoh's second chariot, what did men call out before him?
why: Joseph was placed over all Egypt.
quote: with men calling out before him, “Bow the knee!”
